newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gle Eaux pleases, Lyonnaise disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Gle Eaux pleases, Lyonnaise disappoints.

text.p: Stockmarket analysts welcomed on Friday French utility group Cie Generale des Eaux's move into the telecommunications arena with the entry of blue chip partners into its Cegetel subsidiary.
"It's an excellent operation as it is a good partnership, it brings in cash for development and know-how," Annick Santer, analyst at brokerage Ferri said.
The entry of new partners, apart from their industrial strength, also sets a market value on Cegetel which will bring an exceptional gain for CGE's 1996 results, she added.
Thursday also saw the announcement of rival French utility company Lyonnaise des Eaux of its first-half results, which analysts said were "disappointing."
Brokerage SGE/Delhaye marked down Lyonnaise to "under-perform" from "neutral" but confirmed its buy recommendation on Generale des Eaux, traders said.
The downgrade was partly due to a view that Lyonnaise lacked prospects for a big upturn by the end of the year, they said.
On the Cegetel deal, a second French analyst said, "It's a very good operation." It values CGE's assets, giving it a big profit gain and helps the group pay down debt.
The entry of industry giants British Telecommunications Plc, U.S. SBC and Mannesman AG into the Cegetel company was positive for CGE.
"It lends credibility to its strategy in telecommunications and will gradually change its status in the stockmarket," said Christian Duchesne, analyst at broker EIFB.
But CGE still faces big problems with a 52 billion franc debt mountain and its huge property exposure, analysts said.
Ferri's Santer said CGE was tackling these obstacles through asset sales and with inflows of cash from new partners.
Lyonnaise also had positives on its side, she said.
The company was coming to the end of its problems on construction and was tackling its property exposure. Its stake in Northumbrian Water Plc was also a plus.
But generally, CGE was viewed as more diversified, with rich potential for growth in new areas, while Lyonnaise' core water business was mature and faced margin pressure.

About half Lyonnaise' sales come from water and half of that came from non-domestic sources, but the profit returns would take some time to feed through, one French analyst said. The first-half result was flattered by the Northumbrian acquisition, the analyst added.
Lyonnaise posted first-half net attributable profit of 635 million francs, up 25 percent. Some analysts had forecast profit of around 700 million francs.
Lyonnaise closed down 5.4 francs at 453.80 francs. Generale des Eaux ended up 10 francs at 562.
